benefit: RapidScreen RS-2000 helped radiologists spot small lung cancers
vendor: Deus Technologies, LLC (listed as Riverain Medical Group in the FDA database)
AI system or service: RapidScreen RS-2000
deployed by: Deus Technologies (reader study with 15 radiologists at Georgetown University Medical Center)
measured against: The same radiologists reading the same films without the system
without the AI: Area under the ROC curve 0.8288, sensitivity 71%
with the AI: Area under the ROC curve 0.8654, sensitivity 78%
costs and harms: The RS-2000 placed 5.3 false positive marks per image, and the radiologists' false positive fraction rose from 21% to 22% with it. FDA notes the potential harm of extra work-ups and interventions for benign lesions, and its panel asked that labeling warn of substantial false positives and false negatives.

benefit: Second Look would have cut missed breast cancers by at least a quarter
vendor: CADx Medical Systems, Inc. (listed as iCAD, Inc. in the FDA database)
AI system or service: Second Look
deployed by: CADx Medical Systems (ROSE-1 study on earlier screening mammograms from 17 institutions and ROSE-2 study at 5 institutions)
measured against: Unaided readings of the same earlier mammograms, which had missed every one of the cancers
without the AI: 306 retrospectively visible false negatives at most
with the AI: At least 80.3 of them estimated to be worked up with the marks
costs and harms: Work-ups rose from 16.6 percent to 17.2 percent, which FDA judged insignificant. The device marks many non-malignant areas. FDA lists indirect risks that it fails to mark some actionable lesions and marks lesions that need no action. In 92 percent of the prospective films, added reading time was 20 percent or less.

benefit: LUMA imaging found more high-grade cervical lesions after colposcopy
AI system or service: LUMA Cervical Imaging System
deployed by: Seven colposcopy centers with 16 colposcopists in the intended use study
measured against: Colposcopy alone in the same women
without the AI: 41 women with CIN 2,3+ found by colposcopy (21.2%)
costs and harms: LUMA-directed biopsies found no high-grade disease in 35 of 193 women, an incremental false-positive rate of 18.1% that missed the 15% goal. FDA describes a trade-off of about four women biopsied unnecessarily for each extra cancer found.

benefit: EPA approves Software CEM to monitor NOx from a paper mill's turbine
AI system or service: Pavilion Technologies Software CEM predictive emission monitoring system (PEMS)
deployed by: MeadWestvaco Coated Board, Inc. (Mahrt Mill)
measured against: Two continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS), the next least costly option under EPA's cost model
with the AI: approximately $51,700 a year for two PEMS with in-house audits
costs and harms: EPA required extra quality assurance as a condition of approval, including monthly three-run relative accuracy audits during the ozone season and a stricter sensor alarm system. The oxygen output failed the correlation test, and the boiler model needs a bias adjustment factor.

benefit: TOTAL Scorecard makes FHA's underwriting more consistent
vendor: Federal Housing Administration (HUD), with contractor Unicon Research Corporation and subcontractor Fair Isaac Corporation
AI system or service: Technology Open to Approved Lenders (TOTAL) Scorecard
deployed by: Federal Housing Administration and its direct endorsement lenders
measured against: The FHA versions of Freddie Mac's Loan Prospector and Fannie Mae's Desktop Underwriter scorecards, used before 2004
without the AI: at times the results of their assessments differed, which resulted in the same loan being accepted by one scorecard and referred by the other
with the AI: TOTAL limits the number of loans that need to be approved manually because it provides consistent automatic underwriting decisions
costs and harms: GAO warned that TOTAL's cut point could let more loans likely to default be accepted automatically instead of referred for manual underwriting. TOTAL did not account for market changes such as lower credit scores and down payment assistance. The lighter paperwork also meant less verification than for manually underwritten applications.

benefit: Braintree's predictive emission monitor passes EPA's tests for NOx
AI system or service: Predictive emission monitoring system (PEMS) on Potter II Unit 3
deployed by: Braintree Electric Light Department (BELD), Norton P. Potter II Station Unit 3
measured against: Hourly NOx readings from a temporary reference method system over the same hours, judged by EPA's three statistical tests
without the AI: A linear correlation coefficient (r) above 0.8 required
with the AI: r = 0.8524 on natural gas and r = 0.9211 on fuel oil
costs and harms: EPA required BELD to run seven extra relative accuracy audits a year with a portable analyzer, about $9,850 a year more than the PEMS alone. With outside contractors the saving against an analyzer shrinks to about 21 percent. When a sensor fails, BELD must report the maximum potential NOx rate until the PEMS is fixed or retrained.

benefit: SmartCEM-75 stands in for NOx analyzers at a Dearborn plant
AI system or service: SmartCEM-75 predictive emission monitoring system (PEMS)
deployed by: Dearborn Industrial Generation (DIG), on boiler Unit BL1100 and turbine Unit GTP1
measured against: Hourly readings from the unit's certified NOx analyzer over the same 720 operating hours, judged by EPA's three statistical tests
without the AI: A linear correlation coefficient (r) above 0.8 required
with the AI: r = 0.9678 over all 720 hours and r = 0.9286 over 98 startup and shutdown hours
costs and harms: EPA required extra accuracy checks of the SmartCEM-75 PEMS on Unit GTP1, seven relative accuracy audits a year with a portable analyzer, which it estimated would add about $9,850 a year. It noted that the annual RATAs are costly. The PEMS still needs these stack checks to confirm its output.

benefit: MammaPrint separated node-negative breast cancers by risk of spread
AI system or service: MammaPrint
deployed by: TRANSBIG consortium (independent validation on tumors from five European centers)
measured against: Clinical risk assessment with Adjuvant on-line
without the AI: Unadjusted hazard ratio of 2.32 (95% CI: 1.35 to 4.00)
with the AI: Hazard ratio of 2.13 (95% CI: 1.19 to 3.82) after adjustment for clinical risk
costs and harms: In the TRANSBIG validation, 191 of 302 patients (63.2%) were classed high risk, yet the positive predictive value for metastatic disease within 5 years was 0.22. The negative predictive value was 0.95, so about one in twenty low risk patients still had distant metastasis within 5 years.

benefit: A risk model lets Philadelphia supervise low-risk probationers lightly
vendor: Richard Berk and colleagues (Berk et al. 2009), with the Philadelphia Adult Probation and Parole Department
AI system or service: Random forests risk forecasting model (modified from Berk et al. 2009)
deployed by: Philadelphia Adult Probation and Parole Department, First Judicial District of Pennsylvania
measured against: Standard regional supervision of people forecast as low risk
without the AI: Almost the same contact as in the previous year
costs and harms: With caseloads of about 400 people, probation officers in the low-intensity group could not invest substantial time in any one person. CrimeSolutions reports no cost information for the program.

benefit: Quick Disability Determinations speed up likely disability claims
vendor: IBM, which originally designed the model according to SSA, with later changes by the Social Security Administration
AI system or service: Quick Disability Determination (QDD) predictive model
deployed by: Social Security Administration with state Disability Determination Services
measured against: SSA's recommended timeframe for QDD claims
with the AI: 18 days on average for all sampled claims and 15 days for allowed claims
costs and harms: Of the 575 sampled claims that the model picked as likely allowances, 38, about 7 percent, were not allowed, 35 of them on medical criteria.

benefit: Auditors credit the ATO's advanced analytics with better compliance
vendor: Australian Taxation Office, Office of the Chief Knowledge Officer (analytics group)
AI system or service: ATO advanced analytics: data-mining and predictive models of the analytics group in the Office of the Chief Knowledge Officer
deployed by: Australian Taxation Office (ATO)
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: not in the sources

benefit: Pathwork Tissue of Origin Test matched the known origin of most tumors
AI system or service: Pathwork Tissue of Origin Test
deployed by: Pathwork Diagnostics (clinical validation at four processing laboratories)
measured against: The available diagnosis for each specimen
with the AI: Agreement for 86.3% of metastatic and 92.0% of primary tumor specimens
costs and harms: Tumors from tissues outside the panel were often falsely matched to a panel tissue, including 48 of 49 endometrial cancers, especially with ovarian cancer, and 22 of 28 esophageal cancers. Overall, 6.2% of results disagreed with the available diagnosis and 4.4% were indeterminate.

benefit: Algebra software shows an uncertain gain in a trial's second year
AI system or service: Cognitive Tutor Algebra I, with an ACT-R-based cognitive model, classroom instruction, and curriculum materials
deployed by: Participating public and Catholic parochial schools in 51 districts across seven states (study sites)
measured against: Schools using their usual algebra curriculum
without the AI: Comparison schools in the same implementation year
with the AI: Second high-school cohort: +0.21 standard deviations; p = .04 before correction, not significant at the Clearinghouse’s corrected threshold of .025
costs and harms: Schools incurred higher adoption costs and needed time for implementation. The trial did not show statistically significant gains in every setting.

benefit: SmartCEM-75 matches a NOx analyzer on a Minnesota turbine
AI system or service: SmartCEM-75 predictive emission monitoring system (PEMS)
deployed by: Great River Energy, Cambridge Station Unit 2
measured against: Hourly readings from the unit's certified NOx analyzer over the same 720 operating hours, judged by EPA's three statistical tests
without the AI: A linear correlation coefficient (r) above 0.8 required
with the AI: r = 0.9521 over all 720 hours and r = 0.8541 over the 542 non-DLN startup and shutdown hours
costs and harms: As a condition of approval GRE must run daily quality checks on the SmartCEM-75 output and monthly three-run relative accuracy audits against a reference analyzer, plus periodic relative accuracy test audits. The letter gives no cost figure.

benefit: NCAR's DICast cuts the error of Xcel's wind forecasts to 10.8%
vendor: National Center for Atmospheric Research (Research Applications Laboratory)
AI system or service: NCAR wind power forecasting system with the DICast adaptive forecast blending engine
deployed by: Xcel Energy
measured against: Xcel's wind forecasts in 2008, before NCAR's system
without the AI: about 18 percent for 18 to 42 hours ahead
costs and harms: Editor's note: The reported savings mechanism is coal-unit decommitment when sustained wind is forecast. A forecast error would leave operators needing replacement generation, so forecast accuracy and dispatch flexibility are consequential constraints.

benefit: ITSS tutoring software raises reading comprehension in two trials
vendor: ITSS developers led by Kausalai Wijekumar (contact at Texas A&M University)
AI system or service: Web-Based Intelligent Tutoring for the Structure Strategy (ITSS)
deployed by: Rural and suburban schools in two US states (grades 4, 5 and 7) in the two rated studies
measured against: Classrooms using the usual language arts curriculum
costs and harms: The WWC reports that ITSS is free to access, but teachers must attend a two-day training and administrators a one-day session, at $2,500 to $8,000 per session depending on attendance. Students spent 30 to 45 minutes a week on ITSS. No harm is reported.

benefit: EasyCell's white cell counts track manual microscopy in FDA's review
AI system or service: EasyCell Cell Locator (EasyCell)
deployed by: Medica Corporation (method comparison study at three sites)
measured against: Manual WBC differential by microscopy on the same specimens
with the AI: Correlation coefficient 0.99 for neutrophils, 0.98 for lymphocytes, 0.97 for eosinophils and 0.93 for monocytes
costs and harms: In flagging abnormal slides, EasyCell had 72% specificity overall, so it flagged some slides as abnormal that manual reading found normal. It skipped 0.66% of cells between fields of view, which the hazard analysis deemed acceptable.

benefit: SmartCEM-75 models match NOx analyzers on eight Houston turbines
AI system or service: SmartCEM-75 predictive emission monitoring systems (PEMS), one model per turbine
deployed by: NRG Texas Power (NRG Energy), T.H. Wharton Generating Station Units THW31 to THW34 and THW41 to THW44
measured against: Hourly readings from certified NOx analyzers on the same units over 720 operating hours each, judged by EPA's three statistical tests
without the AI: A linear correlation coefficient (r) above 0.8 required
with the AI: r = 0.936 to r = 0.999 across the eight units
costs and harms: NRG must keep running relative accuracy audits on the SmartCEM-75 systems, monthly from 2010 until EPA cut them to quarterly in May 2025, and report the results electronically. The letters give no cost figure.

benefit: DreamBox Learning lifts early math scores in a San Jose trial
AI system or service: DreamBox Learning (adaptive online K-5 mathematics program)
deployed by: Rocketship Education (three charter elementary schools in San Jose, California)
measured against: Students randomly assigned to an online literacy program during the same lab time
without the AI: 156.20 (comparison group mean, MAP overall math score)
costs and harms: A DreamBox Learning license cost $20 per student per year, or $7,000 per year for a whole school.

benefit: MelaFind caught nearly all melanomas at low specificity
AI system or service: MelaFind
deployed by: Seven dermatology sites in the blinded study (Protocol 20061) and physicians in a web-based reader study (Protocol 20063)
measured against: Study dermatologists' specificity on the same lesions
costs and harms: The advisory panel worried that a negative MelaFind reading could lead a dermatologist to skip a biopsy of a suspicious lesion, causing a false negative and delayed care. MelaFind's specificity was 10.6%. Of lesions that it could not evaluate, 18.7% were melanomas or high-grade lesions.

benefit: PredPol maps cut property crime per patrol minute in an LAPD trial
vendor: PredPol (later Geolitica), from the ETAS model of George Mohler and colleagues
AI system or service: Epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) crime forecasting model, known as PredPol (later Geolitica)
deployed by: Los Angeles Police Department (Foothill, North Hollywood and Southwest divisions)
measured against: Patrols sent to boxes chosen by LAPD crime analysts
with the AI: An average 7.4 percent reduction in crime volume per thousand minutes of patrol time
costs and harms: The Los Angeles Inspector General noted that PredPol may increase police presence or enforcement in hotspot areas, though it found most visits very short. It noted indirect costs for the Palantir dashboard that tracked PredPol, not broken out from the overall contract. Self-reported patrol time could inflate the dosage figures.

benefit: Federal court approves Axcelerate for three million emails
AI system or service: Axcelerate software by Recommind (predictive coding)
deployed by: MSL Group (defendant), with its counsel Jackson Lewis LLP
measured against: Linear manual review or keyword searches
costs and harms: Under the protocol MSL's attorneys had to review at least 500 documents in each of up to seven iterative training rounds. The judge noted that computer-assisted review is not perfect, and the plaintiffs objected to the rulings.

benefit: Virginia court lets defendants use predictive coding over objections
vendor: Not named in the order or in the defendants' memorandum
AI system or service: Predictive coding
deployed by: Landow Aviation Limited Partnership, Landow Aviation I, Inc. and Landow & Company Builders, Inc. (defendants)
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: Counsel for a number of parties objected to the proposed use of predictive coding. The defendants' memorandum puts the reach of predictive coding at upwards of seventy-five percent of the potentially relevant documents, so it does not claim to find all of them.

benefit: Passport photo FR matching exposes otherwise hidden identity fraud
vendor: A commercial supplier of the biometric algorithm (not named in the report)
AI system or service: Australian Passport Office facial recognition (FR) matching of applicants' photos against its image database (one-to-many)
deployed by: Australian Passport Office, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: Reviewing matches takes officers' time. A low threshold adds photos to review, and a high threshold may exclude true matches. A 2008 review warned that the threshold could cause an unacceptably high false rejection rate. The disaster recovery plan did not cover the matching system.

benefit: EPA lets Pavilion8 PEMS stand in for NOx analyzers in Arkansas
vendor: Rockwell Automation (maker of Pavilion8, which the letter names only as a product)
AI system or service: Pavilion8 Software PEMS (predictive emission monitoring systems) on Units G1 through G7
deployed by: Arkansas Electric Cooperative Corporation (AECC), Harry L. Oswald Generating Station
measured against: Certified hardware NOx analyzers (CEMS) on the same turbines
with the AI: Relative accuracy of 1.38% to 3.15% across the seven units, with all three statistical tests passed
costs and harms: not in the sources

benefit: MarginProbe helped surgeons remove cancer left at lumpectomy margins
AI system or service: MarginProbe System
deployed by: Surgical sites in the randomized trial in Israel and the United States (596 women undergoing lumpectomy)
measured against: Standard care in the randomized control arm
without the AI: 25.8% of patients had a further excision
costs and harms: Device use removed more tissue, 92.7 against 69.9 cubic centimeters, and FDA could not say whether this worsened breast appearance. Per margin, the device's specificity was 46.4%, against 83.4% for standard care. One wound infection requiring hospitalization was possibly device-related. Conversions to mastectomy were 18 against 13, which FDA did not attribute to the device.

benefit: Court credits H5 review of almost 12 million records as efficient
AI system or service: H5's computer-assisted, algorithm-driven document review (proprietary technology)
deployed by: Qualcomm Incorporated and its co-defendants, through their counsel Cooley LLP, with contract reviewers from Black Letter Discovery
measured against: Manual review of the records
costs and harms: The H5 review cost $2,829,349.10. Black Letter attorneys then billed $391,928.91 for 6,949.5 hours of review of the documents that H5 marked responsive.

benefit: Amputee with 48 years of phantom limb pain reaches pain-free periods
vendor: Chalmers University of Technology, Biomedical Engineering Division (academic lab; study part-funded by Integrum AB)
AI system or service: Phantom motor execution: BioPatRec myoelectric pattern recognition (LDA and MLP classifiers) driving augmented/virtual reality and a racing game
deployed by: Chalmers University of Technology and Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg (inferred from author affiliations; the paper does not name the treatment site)
measured against: the patient's pain after 48 years of conventional treatments (mirror therapy, drugs, acupuncture, hypnosis)
without the AI: constant burning pain of an intensity of 3 on a scale from 0 to 10 (SF-MGPQ)
with the AI: gradually reduced to complete pain-free periods
costs and harms: BioPatRec's offline accuracy in telling the man's movements apart was low at the start of treatment, so each task used only a few movements. After week 15, his real-time accuracy in a motion test was 75%.

benefit: Court upholds Biomet's predictive coding review under discovery rules
vendor: Recommind, maker of Axcelerate (the order names the service as Axelerate and names no company)
AI system or service: Axelerate predictive coding service (the order's spelling of Axcelerate)
deployed by: Biomet (defendant), with its e-discovery vendor and eight contract attorneys
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: Biomet's e-discovery costs stood at about $1.07 million and were expected to total $2 million to $3.25 million. The review used a predictive coding service and eight contract attorneys. The court put a restart with predictive coding over all 19.5 million documents in the low seven figures.

benefit: VITEK MS identified microbes from patient cultures in five labs
AI system or service: VITEK MS (MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry with the Advanced Spectrum Classifier)
deployed by: Five US clinical microbiology laboratories in the prospective clinical study
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: In the clinical study VITEK MS gave a single wrong identification for 54 of 7068 isolates and no identification for 229. FDA names incorrect identification of a pathogen as the device's main risk. It notes that a no-identification result may delay identification and lead to further testing.

benefit: A listening Reading Tutor beats silent reading in a trial
AI system or service: Project LISTEN's Reading Tutor (speech-recognition reading tutor)
deployed by: Two elementary schools in an affluent suburban school district (not named)
measured against: Sustained silent reading in class during the same daily period
without the AI: 471.49 (comparison group mean, Woodcock Reading Mastery Test total reading composite)
costs and harms: Each student spent about 19 hours in a supervised computer lab, time that otherwise went to silent reading, and a school-provided monitor supervised the lab.

benefit: Nest thermostats trim electricity use in Oregon heat-pump homes
AI system or service: Nest Learning Thermostat (heat pump control)
deployed by: Energy Trust of Oregon pilot, installed by CLEAResult in 185 heat-pump-heated homes
measured against: 299 comparison homes from the same pool without a Nest
with the AI: 781 kWh a year less, 4.7% of total electric usage
costs and harms: Eleven of the 185 thermostats were removed for technical problems, and 22 more needed a second visit to work properly. Another 37 homes were disqualified on site for technical reasons. Energy Trust installed the thermostats free of charge, and the evaluation leaves open whether the measure meets its cost-effectiveness requirements.

benefit: UK live subtitles by respeaking are accurate but late, Ofcom finds
vendor: Not named (speech recognition software used by subtitling providers)
AI system or service: Live subtitling by respeakers using speech recognition software, alongside stenographers
deployed by: BBC, ITV, Channel 4, Channel 5 and Sky and their subtitling providers
measured against: The 98% accuracy threshold that Ofcom's external reviewers treat as acceptable
costs and harms: Respoken subtitles lagged about 6 to 7 seconds behind speech, against Ofcom's 3-second guideline. Delays peaked at 24 seconds and caused omissions and misreporting. Recognition errors made up 37% of errors, such as “be given to ayatollahs” for “be given to our toddlers”. One fifth of programs fell below the quality threshold.

benefit: Machine translation lifts cross-border sales on eBay
AI system or service: eBay Machine Translation (eMT), an in-house statistical machine-learning translation system
deployed by: eBay
measured against: U.S. exports on eBay to destinations that did not receive the change, before and after eBay replaced Bing Translator with eMT
without the AI: Exports with Bing Translator before May 2014
costs and harms: Export revenue rose less than quantity, by 13.1% to 17%, because average selling prices of U.S. exports fell slightly, possibly from more competition among U.S. exporters. By majority vote, three experts did not accept 8.6% of eMT's translations of the 500 most frequent queries.

benefit: Court lets Bridgestone use predictive coding over IBM's objection
AI system or service: Predictive coding
deployed by: Bridgestone Americas, Inc. (plaintiff), with its attorneys, experts and the companies doing the work
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: IBM objected that predictive coding after a search-term screen was unfair and an unwarranted change to the court's original management order. The judge said he was letting Bridgestone switch horses in midstream, so openness and transparency were of critical importance. IBM was between a third and half through its manual review.

benefit: Cologuard caught more colorectal cancers than a standard stool test
AI system or service: Cologuard
deployed by: Exact Sciences (DeeP-C study at 90 sites in the United States and Canada)
measured against: A commercial fecal immunochemical test (OC FIT-CHEK) in the same adults
costs and harms: Cologuard's specificity was lower than FIT's, 86.6% against 94.9%. For 100,000 people, FDA expects 9,005 more false-positive results than with FIT and 61 more adverse events from follow-up colonoscopy. Cologuard detected 42.4% of advanced adenomas.

benefit: Chicago's model would have found food violations 7.5 days earlier
vendor: City of Chicago Department of Innovation and Technology with the Department of Public Health, Allstate Insurance data scientists and the Civic Consulting Alliance
AI system or service: Food Inspection Forecasting (predictive analytics model, open-sourced in R)
deployed by: Chicago Department of Public Health
measured against: the Department of Public Health's normal inspection order during the September-October 2014 pilot
without the AI: 55 percent (141 establishments) of those with critical violations found in the first month during normal operations
with the AI: 69 percent (178 establishments) found in the first half of work; violations found on average 7 and a half days earlier
costs and harms: Editor's note: Inspector identity was an explicit predictor. That feature can capture differences in enforcement as well as differences in restaurant safety; the retained evidence does not separate those mechanisms.

benefit: Tax Court lets taxpayers use predictive coding though the IRS objects
AI system or service: Predictive coding
deployed by: Dynamo Holdings Limited Partnership and Beekman Vista, Inc. (petitioners)
measured against: Review under the Commissioner's approach, a privilege search of all restored data
without the AI: 3.5 million to 7 million documents at a cost of $500,000 to $550,000
with the AI: 200,000 to 400,000 documents at a cost of $80,000 to $85,000
costs and harms: The taxpayers' expert estimated the predictive coding review at $80,000 to $85,000 for 200,000 to 400,000 documents. The Commissioner opposed the method as an unproven technology.

benefit: Ahead 100 EEG test missed its goals but helped rule out injury on CT
AI system or service: BrainScope Ahead 100 (Models CV-100 and M-100)
deployed by: BrainScope (B-AHEAD II study at 11 US emergency department sites)
measured against: Pre-specified endpoints for the lower confidence limits of sensitivity and specificity
without the AI: Lower limits above 78% for sensitivity and 50% for specificity
with the AI: Sensitivity 78.5% and specificity 48.6%, with the endpoints missed
costs and harms: The Ahead 100 classified 25 of 116 patients with injury on CT as negative, and 224 of 436 patients without injury as positive. FDA lists false results from misplaced electrodes, and delayed or unnecessary treatment from hardware or software failure, as risks. It required labeling statements to mitigate potential false negative outputs.

benefit: Bank's network tool links a third company to suspected money laundering
vendor: Bank F (anonymized subsidiary and regional head office of a large global bank); the report names no vendor
AI system or service: Bank F network (graph) analytics solution implemented in Hong Kong in 2013
deployed by: Bank F, Hong Kong
measured against: Bank F's earlier manual review of documentation for signatories, before the network analytics tool
without the AI: manual approaches to reviewing documentation for signatories, which the report calls the only means to make these connections
with the AI: the tool linked Company C to Company A through shared phone numbers and email addresses
costs and harms: The authors do not assess costs or harms, including any to the customers whose relationships the bank reviewed.

benefit: Some subprime borrowers get lower-priced credit at LendingClub
AI system or service: LendingClub rating-grade model (grades A to G)
deployed by: LendingClub
measured against: classification of borrowers by traditional credit criteria
without the AI: classified as subprime by traditional criteria
with the AI: slotted into “better” loan grades, which allowed them to get lower-priced credit
costs and harms: The authors note a risk of disparate treatment and fair lending violations from alternative data and algorithms. They note that consumer privacy may be compromised when insurance claims, utility bills, bank account transactions and social network details are used without consent. The 2023 paper notes lenders that buy a vendor's rating mechanism without understanding their own black box.

benefit: Screening Medicare claims helps catch $654.8 million in 2015
vendor: Contractors engaged by CMS (the report lists 'Developing Contractor Costs' and 'Modeling Contractor Costs' without naming firms)
AI system or service: Fraud Prevention System (FPS)
deployed by: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS)
measured against: the FPS's identified savings in the previous year, 2014
without the AI: identified savings from the previous year ($454.0 million in Table 1)
costs and harms: Costs for 2015 were an estimated $57.1 million, including $19.5 million for a developing contractor and $4.8 million for a modeling contractor. The sources contain no account of a burden on providers or beneficiaries from denied claims or suspended payments.

benefit: Global Fishing Watch helps Kiribati fine a vessel's owner US$1 million
AI system or service: Global Fishing Watch (AIS-based fishing detection using machine learning)
deployed by: Government of Kiribati
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: Editor's note: The retained account explicitly notes that vessels could turn off AIS. A detection method based on those tracks cannot inspect an absent transmission in the same way.

benefit: Return Review Program catches refund fraud that older filters missed
vendor: Internal Revenue Service (Information Technology organization and Office of Research, Applied Analytics, and Statistics)
AI system or service: IRS Return Review Program (RRP) identity-theft models
deployed by: Internal Revenue Service
measured against: The older Electronic Fraud Detection System identity-theft models
without the AI: $60 million (1.5%) of confirmed identity-theft refunds selected only by the older system
with the AI: $1.88 billion (47.8%) selected only by the Return Review Program models
costs and harms: Returns that only the Return Review Program selected in 2015 had a 28.6% false detection rate. Wrongly selected taxpayers can face refund delays. The IRS disabled one rule that was selecting legitimate returns. By March 2018 the IRS had spent about $419 million on the program. In 2014 two of its servers were still open to the Heartbleed bug.

benefit: Nest thermostats cut gas heating use in Oregon homes by about 6%
AI system or service: Nest Learning Thermostat (second generation)
deployed by: Energy Trust of Oregon pilot with NW Natural customers, run by CLEAResult (self-installed thermostats in homes with gas furnaces)
measured against: About 1,000 randomly selected NW Natural customers who were not contacted
with the AI: About 34 therms a year saved, 6.0% of heating usage
costs and harms: Energy Trust paid a $200 rebate on each thermostat, so participants paid $19. Homes given the Honeywell Lyric used 4–5% more gas, 24–29 therms a year. Close to 10% of units were returned, and some failed or proved incompatible.

benefit: Federal court approves a TAR protocol agreed by Rio Tinto and Vale
vendor: Relativity (Relativity Assisted Review) and Deloitte (Dynamic Review), as the parties' letter attached to the opinion names the tools
AI system or service: Relativity Assisted Review (Rio Tinto) and Deloitte's Dynamic Review (Vale), under a stipulated predictive coding protocol
deployed by: Rio Tinto plc (plaintiff), with its vendor Precision Discovery, and Vale S.A. (defendant)
measured against: Keyword searches or manual review
costs and harms: The judge warns that holding TAR to a higher standard than keywords or manual review discourages parties, who may fear spending more in motion practice than the review saves. Under the agreed protocol each side must build a control set by random sampling and have a subject matter expert review it.

benefit: Irish court backs predictive coding for 680,809 bank documents
vendor: Not named in the judgment (the bank's expert took his target f-measure from Symantec, the provider of the Clearwell system)
AI system or service: Technology assisted review using predictive coding
deployed by: Irish Bank Resolution Corporation and its solicitors, in discovery
measured against: Manual (linear) review of the 680,809 documents
without the AI: 9 months at a cost of €2 m by the bank's solicitor's estimate, or 113 days at €220,000 by the defendants' expert's
with the AI: less than 10% of the 680,809 documents would need to be manually reviewed
costs and harms: The defendants objected that technology assisted review will not capture all relevant documents and that its cut-off point will lead to the omission of relevant documents. The bank's expert accepted that no method of identification is guaranteed to return all relevant documents.

benefit: Inspections guided by nEmesis find more venues graded no better than C
vendor: University of Rochester (Adam Sadilek, Henry Kautz and colleagues)
AI system or service: nEmesis (SVM language model over geotagged tweets with a web interface for inspectors)
deployed by: Southern Nevada Health District
measured against: Venues inspected under the standard SNHD protocol in the same three months, with inspectors blind to which venues nEmesis chose
without the AI: 6 demerits per inspection and 7 venues graded C or worse in the control arm
with the AI: 9 demerits per inspection and 11 venues graded C or worse in the nEmesis arm
costs and harms: A 2025 systematic review that covers nEmesis warns that social media data can be unreliable, since posts may reflect anecdotes, rumors or panic, which makes false alarms hard to tell from real outbreaks. The sources report no measured cost or harm from the Las Vegas trial.

benefit: People with low vision complete more daily tasks with OrCam readers
AI system or service: OrCam MyEye, MyEye 2 and OrCam Read (camera-based optical character and object recognition with audio output)
deployed by: Study clinics: an ophthalmology department in the United States (2015); Bartiméus and Royal Dutch Visio, two low-vision rehabilitation centers in Amsterdam; five vision rehabilitation centers; UC Davis Ophthalmology; NIH Clinical Center
measured against: the same patients' best-corrected visual acuity without the device
without the AI: a mean of 2.5 of 10 daily-living tasks completed
with the AI: a mean of 9.5 of 10 tasks with the device at the first visit
costs and harms: In the Dutch study the patients who stopped using the device most often cited other text-to-speech tools such as Seeing AI, the price or missing features.

benefit: Occupants vote to adjust socially driven HVAC to their comfort
vendor: Building Robotics, LLC (named in the evaluation as the technology provider)
AI system or service: Socially driven HVAC optimization software
deployed by: U.S. General Services Administration (Federal Building and U.S. Courthouse, Phoenix)
measured against: The building's previous fixed-range temperature control
with the AI: 83% of occupants reported being more satisfied with their thermal environment
costs and harms: Energy savings alone are not expected to cover subscription costs of up to $0.60 per square foot per year. The technology required heavy scrutiny by GSA's IT security team, which adds installation time. Four users made 41% of the warm-space requests, and the technology was eventually turned off for the users in one zone.

benefit: Subscribing to GLAD alerts lowers deforestation risk in Africa by 18%
vendor: University of Maryland GLAD laboratory (Hansen et al.)
AI system or service: GLAD (Global Land Analysis and Discovery) Landsat deforestation alerts on Global Forest Watch
deployed by: World Resources Institute (Global Forest Watch) and alert subscribers
measured against: average 2011–2016 deforestation levels, with areas lacking alert subscribers as the counterfactual across 22 tropical countries
with the AI: probability of deforestation in Africa decreased by 18%; no effect on other continents
costs and harms: Neither the developers nor the World Resources Institute reports costs or harms from the alerts.

benefit: Flint uses a prediction model to find homes with hazardous water pipes
vendor: University of Michigan (Jacob Abernethy, Alex Chojnacki, Arya Farahi, Eric Schwartz, Jared Webb)
AI system or service: ActiveRemediation, combining XGBoost predictions, a hierarchical Bayesian spatial model, and active learning
deployed by: City of Flint (FAST Start service-line replacement program)
measured against: The recorded sequence of inspection and replacement work in a simulation
costs and harms: Residents and officials also sought broad coverage and certainty about individual homes. These priorities could change the order of excavation.

benefit: Tailgating alerts from Mobileye fall in New York taxis
AI system or service: Mobileye aftermarket warning system, with a black box recorder added for the trial
deployed by: A fleet of mostly yellow taxis licensed by the TLC, in the TLC's Vehicle Safety Technology Pilot
measured against: Alert rates in the same fleet early in the trial
without the AI: 100 alerts for each 100 miles traveled (or one alert per mile) in July 2015
with the AI: between 20 and 40 alerts per 100 miles starting in January 2016
costs and harms: The TLC lists Mobileye's cost at $1,050 to $1,100 per vehicle upfront and $28 to $35 a month with the black box. Crash rates for the fitted vehicles did not show a clear decline.

benefit: English court approves predictive coding for 3 million documents
AI system or service: Predictive coding software
deployed by: MWB Business Exchange Ltd (second claimant), with the agreement of all parties
measured against: A full manual review of over 3 million documents
with the AI: £181,988 plus monthly hosting costs of £15,717, to £469,049 plus monthly hosting costs of £20,820
costs and harms: The predictive coding software itself was estimated to cost between £181,988 and £469,049, plus monthly hosting charges, and Master Matthews noted that manual review might still add costs once the software had done its best.

benefit: Exomiser ranks gene variants to help diagnose rare disease in England
vendor: Queen Mary University of London (Exomiser team led by Damian Smedley)
AI system or service: Exomiser phenotype-driven variant prioritization (machine-learning-assisted scoring and ranking)
deployed by: Genomics England and NHS Genomic Medicine Centers
measured against: the virtual panel-based pipeline (applied gene panels) alone
without the AI: A total of 322 (66%) of the 490 diagnoses that were based on SNVs or indels from the genomes were made with the virtual panel–based pipeline
with the AI: diagnoses were detected in 77% of the top-ranked candidate variants, in 86% of the top three candidates, and in 88% of the top five candidates
costs and harms: The Exomiser team and Genomics England report no costs or harms, and the record has no comparable incident.

benefit: Court orders predictive coding at £132,000 over a keyword search
AI system or service: Predictive coding
deployed by: BCA Trading Ltd and the other respondents
measured against: A keyword search approach to disclosure
without the AI: at least £250,000 (and indeed I believe that figure may even reach £338,000 on a worst case scenario)
costs and harms: Predictive coding was itself expected to cost about £132,000. The petitioner was wary of it, and the registrar acknowledged concern that the new method may not be as effective as traditional but more expensive methods.

benefit: Superpower Glass briefly raises social scores of children with autism
vendor: Stanford University (Wall lab, Division of Systems Medicine and Department of Computer Science)
AI system or service: Superpower Glass: Google Glass with a real-time machine-learning facial emotion classifier and companion smartphone app
deployed by: Participating families at home under the Stanford studies
measured against: applied behavioral analysis therapy alone (treatment as usual)
costs and harms: Access depended on the child tolerating the glasses and the family sustaining repeated sessions. Home lighting and face pose could also reduce the reliability of the emotion cues.

benefit: Tax Court finds a response to the IRS by predictive coding complete
AI system or service: Predictive coding algorithm
deployed by: Dynamo Holdings Limited Partnership and Beekman Vista, Inc. (petitioners)
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: The 95% recall setting returned many nonresponsive documents, at a precision of 3%, and the Commissioner kept 5,796 of about 180,000. After the second seed set, the model was not performing well, so the Commissioner coded more sets. The Commissioner said that 1,353 documents with Boolean hits were left out, and the court assumed that the response was flawed.

benefit: A texting assistant helps more admitted students enroll at Georgia State
AI system or service: Pounce, AdmitHub’s SMS assistant with supervised learning and a Georgia State knowledge base
deployed by: Georgia State University
measured against: Usual enrollment support among students already committed to Georgia State
costs and harms: The service required staff to maintain answers and resolve difficult questions. Students could opt out of messages.

benefit: Embrace wristband alerts a mother, who calls paramedics
AI system or service: Empatica Embrace wrist-worn seizure detection (electrodermal activity and accelerometer, on-board algorithm) with the Alert smartphone app
deployed by: not in the sources
measured against: seizures recorded during more than 6,500 hours of monitoring of 135 patients (device test reported by IEEE Spectrum)
with the AI: the device correctly identified nearly every single seizure, with a false alarm rate below that of the seizure frequency for most individuals
costs and harms: False alarms and broken connectivity could reduce the value of monitoring, and seizures without convulsions fell outside the demonstrated detection capability.

benefit: QVCAD cut reading time for breast ultrasound by a third
AI system or service: QVCAD System
deployed by: QView Medical (reader study with 18 radiologists on 185 automated breast ultrasound cases)
measured against: The same radiologists reading the same cases without QVCAD
costs and harms: Used alone, the software marked about half of the non-cancer exams in dense breasts, with specificity of 49.0% and 52.8%. FDA warns that its marks may lead to extra imaging and biopsies, and that readers who rely on the absence of marks may miss cancers. The reader study recorded no adverse events.

benefit: Victorian court orders TAR for 1.4 million pipeline documents
AI system or service: Predictive coding technology (TAR or Technology Assisted Review)
deployed by: McConnell Dowell Constructors (Aust) Pty Ltd (plaintiff), with the agreement of all parties
measured against: Manual review of 1,400,000 documents at one minute each
without the AI: over 23,000 hours, equating to over 583 working weeks
costs and harms: The parties decided to invest in TAR, and the court expected its implementation to take several months. The court said it would order payment of the Special Referee. A ruling that the court cites notes that no method is guaranteed to find all relevant documents.

benefit: Software flags Swedish children at risk of dyslexia from eye movements
vendor: Karolinska Institutet (Nilsson Benfatto, Öqvist Seimyr and colleagues); two authors hold equity in Optolexia
AI system or service: Eye-tracking during reading with a support-vector-machine classifier (SVM-RFE, 48 features)
deployed by: None in the sources (research study)
measured against: chance-level classification on the same cross-validation (and random feature selection)
costs and harms: The high accuracy may overstate performance in ordinary school screening, because the study compared selected high-risk and low-risk children. Schools Week reported that a privacy group raised concerns about how pupils' data might be used.

benefit: Auditors use an Alice email to stop overlapping road tenders in Brazil
vendor: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) with the Ministério da Transparência e Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU), in-house
AI system or service: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais), TCU/CGU text-analysis and data cross-checking robot
deployed by: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU), Goiás unit
measured against: TCU auditors reading the roughly 200 federal tender notices published each day by hand
without the AI: seria muito custoso porque são, em média, 200 editais por dia
with the AI: Os auditores do Tribunal de Contas da União recebem pontualmente às 19h um e-mail de Alice. São os resumos das centenas de contratações federais publicadas naquele dia.
costs and harms: An interviewee said that TCU auditors complained that Alice's messages overloaded their email boxes and that the court lacked staff to check every alert. Alice's accuracy fell from 88.27% in testing to 73.91% in later auditing.

benefit: Swedish risk model finds more errors in parental-benefit claims
vendor: Försäkringskassan (Swedish Social Insurance Agency), Urvalsanalys unit
AI system or service: Försäkringskassan's risk-based selection profile (urvalsprofil) for checks of temporary parental benefit, run through the RaKuR infrastructure
deployed by: Försäkringskassan (Swedish Social Insurance Agency)
measured against: Claims picked at random for checks in 2017
costs and harms: The risk-selected checks failed ISF's equal-treatment test. Among the errors they found, people with a foreign background made up 47.6%, against 28% among errors found at random. Women made up 65.4%, against 55.8%. ISF also found the legal basis for risk-based selection unclear.

benefit: Screen-in calls more accurate with the Allegheny Family Screening Tool
vendor: Not named in the evaluation (built for the Allegheny County Department of Human Services)
AI system or service: Allegheny Family Screening Tool (AFST), a predictive risk model that scores child welfare hotline referrals
deployed by: Allegheny County Department of Human Services, Office of Children, Youth and Families (hotline call screeners)
measured against: General protective service referrals before the tool, January 2015 to July 2016
with the AI: Roughly 24 more children each month screened in accurately
costs and harms: Accuracy for screened-out children may have slightly decreased, with roughly 11 more children a month screened out inaccurately, a result not statistically significant. Carnegie Mellon researchers found that the tool flagged a disproportionate share of Black children for mandatory investigation, and the county confirmed a glitch that showed wrong scores for more than two years.

benefit: Nest Seasonal Savings trims winter heating in Oregon homes
AI system or service: Nest Seasonal Savings (setpoint and schedule optimization service for Nest thermostats)
deployed by: Energy Trust of Oregon with CLEAResult and Nest, offered to existing Nest owners
measured against: A control group of Nest thermostats from the same population
costs and harms: Over half of the surveyed opt-in participants noticed the temperature changes, and a third of those believed that their homes became less comfortable. Over half overrode some of the settings. Summer cooling savings were only 4 kWh per thermostat, against 12 kWh that Nest reported. Energy Trust paid Nest per participant.

benefit: EyeArt could halve retinal grading and miss no high-risk retinopathy
AI system or service: EyeArt
deployed by: Three NHS diabetic eye screening programs in England (North East London, South East London and Gloucestershire), in a research evaluation run in parallel with usual care
measured against: The current pathway, in which human graders grade every screening episode
with the AI: 15 091/30 405 episodes needing further human grading after EyeArt
costs and harms: At the setting tested, EyeArt's specificity against non-referable retinopathy was 54%, a false-positive rate of 46%, so about half of all episodes, 15,091 of 30,405, would still have gone to human graders.

benefit: Data analytics placement lifts college English completion at SUNY
vendor: Center for the Analysis of Postsecondary Readiness (Community College Research Center and MDRC) with each college
AI system or service: Multiple measures, data analytics placement system (predictive placement algorithms developed at each college)
deployed by: Seven SUNY community colleges: Cayuga, Jefferson, Niagara, Onondaga, Rockland, Schenectady and Westchester
measured against: Students placed by the colleges' standard procedures, mostly ACCUPLACER cut points
without the AI: 28.00% completed a college-level English course in the first semester
costs and harms: Students whom the algorithms bumped down into developmental courses had much lower rates of enrollment in and completion of college-level courses. Implementing the system cost $895,720 for three cohorts, or $70 per student, after planning that lasted a year or longer. Fewer developmental credits more than offset this, for a total of $140 less per student.

benefit: Machine learning helps price Zimbabwe's health financing package
AI system or service: Machine-learning-based optimization tool for pricing interventions in Zimbabwe's results-based financing package (not named in the review)
deployed by: Zimbabwe's results-based financing program under the Ministry of Health and Child Care, with Cordaid as project implementation entity (the review does not say who ran the price reviews)
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: not in the sources

benefit: Public Safety Assessment replaces money bail across New Jersey
vendor: Arnold Ventures (Laura and John Arnold Foundation) with a team of experts
AI system or service: Public Safety Assessment (PSA) with New Jersey's decision-making framework
deployed by: New Jersey Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and New Jersey law enforcement
measured against: Pre-reform trends projected forward in MDRC's interrupted time series
without the AI: 21.9% of people charged with indictable offenses predicted not released or detained after the detention hearing
costs and harms: By the end of 2019 the New Jersey Judiciary had spent or committed $86.2 million on Pretrial Services, whose staff prepare more than 42,000 assessments a year. Since July 2019 the state has paid $22 million a year. Black defendants were more often charged on complaint-warrants and made up 55 percent of the jail population in 2019.

benefit: Restaurants that Google's FINDER flags are more often found unsafe
AI system or service: FINDER (machine-learned foodborne illness detection model)
deployed by: Southern Nevada Health District (Las Vegas) and Chicago Department of Public Health
measured against: all other restaurant inspections conducted in the two cities during the deployment period (BASELINE)
with the AI: 52.3% of FINDER-identified restaurants deemed unsafe (3.06 times as likely)
costs and harms: The authors say that FINDER costs the health departments personnel time spent working with and responding to its signal. Of the restaurants that it flagged, 52.3% were deemed unsafe on inspection, so nearly half were not.

benefit: Veterans flagged by REACH VET attempt suicide less but die as often
vendor: US Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Mental Health and Suicide Prevention
AI system or service: REACH VET (Recovery Engagement and Coordination for Health - Veterans Enhanced Treatment) suicide-risk predictive model and care-enhancement program
deployed by: Veterans Health Administration, all facilities
measured against: veterans in the top 0.1% risk tier during the pre-REACH VET period (March 2014 to December 2015) and subthreshold-risk cohorts, in a triple-difference design
costs and harms: The Fuller Project reported on 30 May 2024 that the model favors men and that officials left military sexual trauma out of its 61 variables. Nextgov reported in 2024 that research found that the model “considered being a white man more of an indicator of potential self-harm than other factors”. Nextgov also reported that a REACH VET 2.0 adding military sexual trauma and intimate partner violence as risk factors was planned for early 2025.

benefit: PowerLook Tomo cut radiologists' reading time on 3D mammograms
AI system or service: iCAD PowerLook Tomo Detection Software
deployed by: iCAD (reader study with 20 radiologists on 240 GE tomosynthesis cases)
measured against: The same radiologists reading the same cases without the software
costs and harms: FDA warns that PowerLook Tomo Detection may raise false-positive or false-negative rates, with false positives leading to unnecessary imaging radiation, biopsy and anxiety. In the reader study average specificity fell from 0.527 to 0.509 with the software.

benefit: Kyukyu VoiceTra translates for ambulance crews across Japan
vendor: NICT (National Institute of Information and Communications Technology) with the Fire and Disaster Management Agency and its Fire Research Center
AI system or service: Kyukyu VoiceTra (救急ボイストラ): multilingual speech-translation app for ambulance crews built on NICT's VoiceTra engine, 15 languages, 46 fixed phrases
deployed by: Fire headquarters across Japan (Sapporo Fire Department from February 2017; Ninomiya Town fire service from 2022)
measured against: the methods that Sapporo ambulance crews used before the app (既存の方法), such as communication boards
with the AI: more than 70% of crews said that both the speed and the quality of communication improved, and more than 90% wanted to keep using the app
costs and harms: The developers' field tests of the general VoiceTra app found that translated exchanges took about twice as long as exchanges in Japanese, which led them to add fixed phrases. No harm to a patient has been reported.

benefit: In 2024 police drop VeriPol, which flagged false robbery reports in 2017
vendor: Universidad Complutense de Madrid and Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, with Spanish National Police officer Miguel Camacho-Collados
AI system or service: VeriPol
deployed by: Spanish National Police (Policía Nacional), Ministry of the Interior
measured against: the average monthly number of false robbery reports detected and closed in June of 2008 to 2016 in the same two cities
without the AI: an average of 3.33 in Murcia and 12.14 in Málaga per June month
with the AI: 25 in Murcia and 39 in Málaga in one week
costs and harms: Editor's note: The original investigation identifies officer-written reports and cites a review of regional coverage and training. The resulting risk of misplaced suspicion is a curatorial inference.

benefit: Facebook's settlement maps shrink the area that volunteers map in Malawi
vendor: Facebook Inc. with CIESIN, Columbia University, and the World Bank Development Data Group
AI system or service: Facebook (Meta) High Resolution Settlement Layer population density maps
deployed by: American Red Cross (Missing Maps) supporting the Measles and Rubella Initiative campaign in Malawi
measured against: mapping the whole national land area without the settlement maps (the normal Missing Maps approach)
costs and harms: Filtering out land that the settlement maps marked as uninhabited could leave small, new or poorly detected settlements off the task list. The developers report a recall of 0.84 for the layer in a rural test area near Blantyre.

benefit: Decoder reads a paralyzed man's brain signals to move an exoskeleton
vendor: CEA-Clinatec (public research institute, not a company) with Grenoble University Hospital
AI system or service: Clinatec epidural wireless brain-machine interface with adaptive decoder driving a four-limb exoskeleton and virtual avatar
deployed by: Clinatec research center / Grenoble University Hospital clinical trial
measured against: intracortical microelectrode brain-computer interfaces reported elsewhere
with the AI: a semi-invasive epidural system that the authors say has similar efficiency
costs and harms: Editor's note: The retained record combines surgically implanted bilateral recorders with two years of training and laboratory safety equipment. Those dependencies make unsupervised everyday mobility an unlikely interpretation of the result.

benefit: Nevisense caught nearly all melanomas at low specificity
AI system or service: Nevisense (electrical impedance spectroscopy with a trained lesion classifier)
deployed by: Dermatology sites in the SIMPS study in Europe and the United States, and 41 US dermatologists in a reader study
measured against: The same dermatologists judging the same lesion images without the device output
costs and harms: The device classified about 69% of lesions without melanoma as positive, and it missed 4.1% of melanomas. Readers' specificity fell by 4% with the device output. FDA names false positives, which can lead to more screening and skin biopsies, and false negatives, which can delay diagnosis. Twelve subjects had device-related events, including bleeding during measurement.

benefit: An autonomous eye exam passed its trial in primary care clinics
AI system or service: IDx-DR
deployed by: Ten primary care sites in the IDx-DR pivotal trial
measured against: Pre-specified FDA performance goals for sensitivity and specificity
costs and harms: The software found 173 of 198 people with more than mild retinopathy and cleared 556 of 621 people without it. FDA names delayed treatment after a false negative as the principal risk, and alarm fatigue after a false positive. Six people with enlarged optic disc cups were not flagged.

benefit: KYield proposes an AI system to prevent catastrophes caused by people
AI system or service: HumCat, powered by the Kyield Operating System (KOS)
deployed by: not in the sources
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: not in the sources

benefit: QuantX gave radiologists a small gain on breast MRI
AI system or service: QuantX
deployed by: Quantitative Insights (reader study with 19 radiologists)
measured against: The same radiologists reading the same cases without QuantX
costs and harms: FDA lists risks of incorrect lesion characterization by QuantX. False-positive results may lead to unnecessary imaging, biopsy or treatment. False-negative results may lead to a wrong diagnosis and delay in disease management. Device failure could lead to absent, delayed or incorrect results.

benefit: Traveler Verification Service matched 98% of photographed passengers
vendor: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (the Inspector General does not name the algorithm's supplier)
AI system or service: Traveler Verification Service (TVS), CBP's facial recognition matching service
deployed by: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Biometric Entry-Exit Program, with airlines at nine airports (Sprint 8 pilot)
measured against: CBP's objective for full implementation in 2021, a match rate of 97%
with the AI: 98 percent average technical match rate, August to December 2017
costs and harms: In December 2017 about 0.03% of match results were false positives and 0.5% false rejects. Travelers under 29 or over 70 matched less often, and U.S. citizens were up to six times more likely to be rejected. Officers ran the cameras and did secondary screening. CBP put the cost of biometric exit through 2025 at about $1.08 billion.

benefit: Advanced RBC Application sorted red cells close to manual microscopy
AI system or service: Advanced RBC Application (CellaVision DM96 and DM1200)
deployed by: CellaVision (method comparison studies at five clinical sites)
measured against: Manual microscopy of the same smears
with the AI: Efficiency 90.6%, sensitivity 85% and specificity 93.6% for schistocytes, target cells, sickle cells, tear drop cells and parasites
costs and harms: For clinically significant red cell findings and parasites, sensitivity against manual microscopy was 85%, so about 15% of positive samples were missed. Size agreement with an automated counter was 81.3%. Skilled operators must verify or correct every suggested result.

benefit: Google's self-driving cars had a lower crash rate in Mountain View
AI system or service: Google self-driving car (test fleet under employee supervision)
deployed by: Google (test fleet on public roads)
measured against: Police-reported crash rates of human drivers in Mountain View
without the AI: 6.06 police-reportable crashes per million vehicle miles traveled
with the AI: 2.19 police-reportable crashes per million vehicle miles traveled
costs and harms: UMTRI counted 11 crashes of self-driving vehicles in autonomous mode through September 2015, with 4 minor injuries in 2 crashes, and found none at fault. It estimated a higher crash rate than for conventional vehicles, 9.1 against 4.1 per million miles, though the confidence intervals overlap.

benefit: OPTiM tests AI monitoring of cameras at two JR Kyushu stations
AI system or service: AI Physical Security Service (AI surveillance-camera service on OPTiM Cloud IoT OS)
deployed by: Kyushu Railway Company (JR Kyushu), trial at two stations
measured against: remote operators who watch many station camera monitors without automated alerts
without the AI: operators check many monitors to support stations
with the AI: AI alerts on the monitor and by email when it detects an anomaly
costs and harms: not in the sources

benefit: A learning controller makes a prosthetic arm easier to use at home
vendor: Center for Bionic Medicine, Shirley Ryan AbilityLab (formerly the Rehabilitation Institute of Chicago), with Northwestern University
AI system or service: Myoelectric pattern recognition control (machine-learning classification of residual-limb EMG) on a custom transhumeral prosthesis built from commercially available parts
deployed by: Center for Bionic Medicine, Shirley Ryan AbilityLab, with home use by trial participants
measured against: The same prosthesis under conventional direct control
without the AI: 137 ± 60.2 seconds for the clothespin relocation task
with the AI: 90.2 ± 39.6 seconds for the clothespin relocation task
costs and harms: Participants noted that the prosthesis sometimes moved unintentionally under pattern recognition control. They recalibrated the pattern recognition control 32.6 times on average over the home trial. One of the eight participants did worse on every outcome measure with pattern recognition and preferred direct control.

benefit: Judge clears New York City's TAR system after in camera review
AI system or service: The City of New York's technology assisted review (predictive coding) software, not named in the opinion
deployed by: City of New York (defendant) and its document review team
measured against: Manual review
costs and harms: The City had spent over $350,000 reviewing more than 100,000 documents and expected about $248,000 more for the plaintiffs' added searches. The review wrongly marked five documents non-responsive and later relabeled 15 responsive documents as non-responsive. The court ordered the City to hand over a random sample of 300 non-responsive documents.

benefit: Google's neural network finds an eighth planet around the star Kepler-90
vendor: Google (Christopher Shallue, Google Brain) with Andrew Vanderburg (University of Texas at Austin)
AI system or service: Deep convolutional neural network for Kepler transit-signal classification (Shallue and Vanderburg)
deployed by: Shallue and Vanderburg, applied to NASA Kepler archival data
measured against: the automated tests and human vetting previously used to verify Kepler signals
without the AI: the weakest signals often are missed using these methods
with the AI: the neural network correctly identified true planets and false positives 96 percent of the time
costs and harms: not in the sources

benefit: Most staff found Insight useful for reviewing hearing decisions
vendor: Staff of SSA's Office of Appellate Operations (SSA's Office of Analytics and Improvements took over the program after its release)
AI system or service: Insight (SSA quality-review software for disability hearing decisions)
deployed by: SSA Office of Appellate Operations and Office of Hearings Operations
measured against: Cases of appellate analysts who did not use Insight, in the appellate office's own study
without the AI: 21.5 percent of non-Insight users' cases returned for quality issues
costs and harms: SSA had spent over $3.4 million on Insight and had not estimated the cost of maintaining it. Seventy-one users thought that its flags had accuracy issues. One user found legal errors that Insight missed. Another said that rewriting decisions after its feedback added processing time.

benefit: Health insurer's datamining model finds more irregular CMU-C files
AI system or service: Data-mining model for after-the-fact checks of CMU-C files
deployed by: Caisses primaires d'assurance maladie (CPAM), all funds since June 2019
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: In 2026 the Défenseur des droits found that the legal framework for the Cnam's bank-statement control of holders of the C2S, the successor to the CMU-C, falls short on privacy and is imperfectly applied. A supervised learning algorithm mainly selects the files. An anomaly rate of about 8% raised doubts about proportionality.

benefit: Datamining lists double the yield of URSSAF audits of small firms
vendor: Agence centrale des organismes de sécurité sociale (Acoss)
AI system or service: Acoss data-mining risk scores (outils de datamining) that list small and medium firms (since 2015) and very small firms (since 2016) for URSSAF accounting audits
deployed by: URSSAF network
measured against: All URSSAF accounting audits of very small firms in 2018, including those picked by data mining
costs and harms: not in the sources

benefit: ContaCT alerts came sooner than usual care in a test on past scans
AI system or service: ContaCT
deployed by: Viz.ai (standalone performance test on archived CT angiograms)
measured against: Usual-care time from CT angiogram to specialist notification in radiology reports
costs and harms: FDA found no major risks because ContaCT runs in parallel with usual care. It lists minor risks: a missed positive scan may delay or misdirect a patient's care, a positive alert may push other patients' images down the queue, and the software could be misused on an unintended population.

benefit: Delhi's face recognition matches 2,930 children without solving a case
vendor: Innefu Labs Pvt Ltd (manufacturer, per The Wire citing the BPR&D Compendium of Equipment); supplied by Pelorus Technologies Pvt Ltd
AI system or service: Delhi Police Facial Recognition System (reported by The Wire as Innefu Labs' AI Vision)
deployed by: Delhi Police (Crime Branch), using Ministry of Women and Child Development Track Child portal data
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: The ministry's counsel told the court that the software sometimes matched photographs of missing boys with girls. The linked Buenos Aires incident concerns another system, and it does not show that the same harm occurred in Delhi.

benefit: Dexcom G6's Urgent Low Soon alert may cut time below 54 mg/dL
AI system or service: Dexcom G6 real-time continuous glucose monitoring system, 'Urgent Low Soon' predictive low glucose alert (also present on the G7 in one independent study)
deployed by: not in the sources
measured against: the same users on the preceding Dexcom G5 system, which had no predictive alert (before-and-after)
without the AI: 1.0 (1.5) percent of time <54 mg/dL on G5 (70 mg/dL low-alert setting, Table 1)
with the AI: 0.6 (1.0) percent of time <54 mg/dL on G6 (70 mg/dL low-alert setting, Table 1)
costs and harms: Repeated or nuisance alerts can make users mute warnings, which removes the opportunity for earlier intervention.

benefit: OsteoDetect helped clinicians find wrist fractures on X-rays
AI system or service: OsteoDetect
deployed by: Imagen Technologies (reader study with 24 clinicians)
measured against: The same clinicians reading the same cases without OsteoDetect
costs and harms: FDA lists false positive and false negative results as the identified risks to health of OsteoDetect, to be mitigated by general and special controls. The sources report no cost figure.

benefit: FAO and Penn State launch Nuru to confirm damage from fall armyworm
AI system or service: PlantVillage Nuru fall armyworm model (machine learning, offline Android app)
deployed by: FAO (Fall Armyworm Monitoring and Early Warning System, FAMEWS) and farmers and extension workers in sub-Saharan Africa
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: In its first two weeks the Nuru beta app underestimated fall armyworm damage, likely because of how the phone was held. Mongabay notes that automated misidentification can still lead to mistakes and that not every small farmer can afford a phone.

benefit: Surgery-length predictions shortened patient waits at Sloan Kettering
vendor: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (Department of Strategy and Innovation)
AI system or service: Memorial Sloan Kettering machine learning surgical case-duration prediction model
deployed by: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
measured against: Cases randomized to the usual EHR estimate with surgeon or scheduler adjustment
costs and harms: A scheduler at Memorial Sloan Kettering had to enter the model's predictions by hand each weekday morning. This manual step limited the trial to two of 14 surgical services. Implementation problems arose only in the model arm. The model may predict poorly when booked procedure codes differ from the operation performed.

benefit: How many eagles IdentiFlight's turbine stops save is disputed
AI system or service: IdentiFlight automated eagle detection and turbine curtailment (camera system with machine-learning classification)
deployed by: Top of the World Windpower Facility, Wyoming
measured against: a control wind facility 15 km away without automated curtailment, before and after the installation
without the AI: increasing at the control site by 113% (51%–218%)
with the AI: the number of fatalities at the treatment site declined by 63% (95% CI = 59%–66%)
costs and harms: Editor's note: The source measures virtual orders. Energy loss and equipment wear are plausible consequences of executing those orders, not measured outcomes of this trial.

benefit: CBP facial comparison at Dulles flags a French-passport impostor
AI system or service: CBP facial comparison biometric system (biometric entry/exit, Traveler Verification Service)
deployed by: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Field Operations, Washington Dulles International Airport
measured against: an officer's visual check of the traveler against the passport photo
without the AI: officials said that the passport may have passed at face value with human inspection
with the AI: the facial comparison reported a mismatch and the traveler was sent to secondary inspection
costs and harms: Editor's note: This case shows that a mismatch led to a consequential search, although a separate identity document corroborated the result here.

benefit: MATRx plus identified apnea patients who did well with a mouthpiece
AI system or service: MATRx plus
deployed by: Zephyr Sleep Technologies (home study in adults with mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea)
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: Participants using MATRx plus reported temporary pain in teeth, jaw and jaw joint, gum irritation, a temporary change in bite and disrupted sleep. After the test, 10.0% of participants still needed further adjustment of their appliance and 3.9% were false positives found at clinical follow-up.

benefit: Camera alerts bring help sooner to residents with dementia who fall
AI system or service: SafelyYou Guardian (SYG): continuous bedroom video monitoring with computer vision fall detection and real-time notification
deployed by: Six memory care facilities in California (not named in the paper)
measured against: Baseline period without regular video review or real-time notification
without the AI: Proportion of fallers on the ground for more than one hour: 31% (8 of 26)
with the AI: No such events in the real-time notification period
costs and harms: Some residents or their representatives declined the bedroom cameras over privacy concerns about video recording, so those residents went unmonitored. The study reports no money figures and no false alarms.

benefit: Software detects more cardiac arrests than Copenhagen dispatchers do
AI system or service: Corti machine-learning call-analysis framework for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest recognition (the peer-reviewed papers describe it only as a machine learning framework, and the EENA report names Corti)
deployed by: Copenhagen Emergency Medical Services, Emergency Medical Dispatch Center Copenhagen
measured against: Dispatchers without alerts in the trial's control group, on confirmed cardiac arrests
with the AI: 85.0% sensitivity for the machine learning alerts alone
costs and harms: The model detected more cardiac arrests but also generated more false alarms: Its specificity was 97.4%, compared with 99.6% for dispatchers without alerts. Giving dispatchers alerts did not significantly improve their recognition rate.

benefit: Nuru may have lifted cassava yield from 0.5 kg to 2–5 kg a plant
vendor: PlantVillage, Pennsylvania State University, with the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA)
AI system or service: PlantVillage Nuru (offline TensorFlow convolutional neural network for cassava disease and pest symptoms on a smartphone)
deployed by: Self Help Africa and Ugunja Resource Center (lead-farmer program in Busia County)
measured against: the same farmer's harvests before she used the Nuru app
costs and harms: Editor's note: The mechanism links visible disease screening to healthier planting material. The same account records certified varieties, spacing advice and market changes without separating their effects.

benefit: Over 100 people charged after South Wales AFR Identify searches
AI system or service: AFR Identify, using NEC's NeoFace facial recognition
deployed by: South Wales Police
measured against: not in the sources
costs and harms: With the newer algorithm, operators rejected the system's matches in 136 of 1,524 searches, and the system rejected 68% of probe images as poor in quality. Officers researched possible matches themselves. One man with deformed features appeared in results “all the time”. The searches were an extra task for an existing unit.

benefit: Neural network finds 72 missed pulses from a repeating fast radio burst
vendor: University of California, Berkeley (Berkeley SETI Research Center, Breakthrough Listen)
AI system or service: Convolutional neural network for FRB pulse detection (Zhang et al., Breakthrough Listen / Berkeley SETI Research Center)
deployed by: Breakthrough Listen, on Green Bank Telescope data
measured against: the conventional search algorithm previously run on the same observation
with the AI: 72 new pulses, totaling 93 pulses in five hours
costs and harms: A 2023 search of the first 30 minutes of the same data by astronomers at the University of Amsterdam and ASTRON re-detected 30 of the 46 candidates from the neural network. The 16 that it missed were low signal-to-noise pulses whose astrophysical nature is unclear.

benefit: Medicare credits ContaCT with faster stroke alerts in a payment review
AI system or service: ContaCT (Viz LVO algorithm with Viz Hub and Viz View)
deployed by: US hospitals using ContaCT, including SkyRidge Medical Center, Wellstar, Methodist Le Bonheur Healthcare and Mount Sinai Health System
measured against: Usual-care notification time in the retrospective test on past scans that FDA reviewed, as cited by CMS
costs and harms: FDA lists minor risks of ContaCT. A failure to prioritize a scan with a positive finding may delay a patient's management. A false positive costs a specialist a small amount of time to review and disregard the notification.

benefit: Autopilot kept Teslas centered for miles in CR's first ranking
AI system or service: Autopilot, as fitted to the Tesla Model X, Model S and Model 3 (2018)
deployed by: Tesla (fitted to the Model X, Model S and Model 3)
measured against: Nissan's ProPilot Assist and Volvo's Pilot Assist in the same Consumer Reports tests
without the AI: The Nissan and Volvo systems had trouble with curvy or hilly roads, and they had frequent lane departures.
with the AI: Autopilot and Super Cruise were the clear winners.
costs and harms: Consumer Reports found that these systems introduce new safety risks. Autopilot waited 24 seconds to warn an inattentive driver and scored 1 of 5 for keeping the driver engaged. Its lane keeping makes drivers easily overreliant. It let drivers use it on small, curvy roads with poor lane markings, where it operated erratically.

benefit: LensHooke X1 let lay users measure sperm concentration accurately
AI system or service: LensHooke X1 and X1 PRO Semen Quality Analyzer
deployed by: Bonraybio (user performance study with 100 lay users at three evaluation sites)
measured against: A point-of-care professional testing the same samples on the SQA-V reference analyzer
with the AI: Sperm concentration slope 0.98 and R2 0.98, motility slope 0.98 and R2 0.95, morphology slope 0.78 and R2 0.73
costs and harms: not in the sources

benefit: PAWS-directed patrols remove over 1,000 snares in Cambodia
vendor: Harvard University and University of Southern California (Milind Tambe and colleagues), with WWF, WCS and Uganda Wildlife Authority co-authors
AI system or service: PAWS (Protection Assistant for Wildlife Security), enhanced iWare-E predictive model with Gaussian-process uncertainty and game-theoretic patrol planning
deployed by: WWF Cambodia with Cambodia Ministry of Environment rangers, Srepok Wildlife Sanctuary
measured against: the rangers' usual monthly snare removal without PAWS
without the AI: two or three hundred snares in an average month
